personas.description: Public-integrity journalist investigating Mexican government contract awards.
Compliance analyst screening suppliers for procurement due diligence.

jobs_to_be_done.description: Identify who receives public money via Mexican government contracts.
Assess whether a recipient is a legitimate, registered operating company.

requirements.description: Ingest public procurement award records (e.g., CompraNet) with contractor name, RFC, amount, and contracting entity.
Normalize and deduplicate contractor identities across sources into a single canonical entity record.
Attach authority-sourced legitimacy signals: RFC/SAT registration, SAT 69-B EFOS list status, and registry data.
Render a transparent legitimacy scorecard per entity with per-signal source citation and retrieval timestamp.

constraints: Public read-only sources only; no authenticated scraping or paywalled data.
Mexican federal data-protection law (LFPDPPP) applies; process only publicly disclosed data.
Every claim must carry source URL, publisher, and retrieval timestamp.
No automated publication; human review required before any output is released.
Unknown or unverifiable source domains are quarantined for review, never used as evidence.

authority_policy.jurisdiction: Mexico (federal), with secondary cross-checks against United States public sanctions and corporate-registry data.

trusted_publishers.rationale: Primary source of record for federal contract awards and open procurement data.
Authoritative for RFC validity, EFOS/DEOS lists, and international sanctions screening.

non_goals: Making or publishing legal accusations of wrongdoing against named parties.
Building paid, credentialed, or real-time data feeds.
Covering state or municipal procurement in the initial release.
Automated outreach, publication, or notification to third parties.
